solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Party-pooper overindulges on wine

parts.note: to spoil a child is to overindulge it, so overindulges gives spoils
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A guest complains that someone at the party is drinking far too much wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A party-pooper is someone who dampens others' fun, exactly what a killjoy of this kind does.

clue.text: Toast ex-Formula 1 champion

definitions.meaning: the German drinking toast, used as 'cheers' when glasses are raised
Alain ..., French racing driver and four-time Formula 1 world champion

explanation.definitionFit: It is the German word said when raising a glass, and also the surname of the French four-time world champion driver.

clue.text: Bill, popular singer

parts.note: something popular or fashionable is said to be in
a singer can be referred to as a voice, as in 'a fine voice in the choir'

explanation.surface: A poster advertises a bill featuring a well-loved vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a written request for payment, the document a supplier sends after a sale.

clue.text: Waterproof sheets for covering up fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for the sheets is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tarps, short for tarpaulins, are waterproof sheets used for covering things

explanation.surface: Tarpaulins are laid over a catch of fish to keep it covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery fish of the herring family, common in European waters.

clue.text: Man in debt adores malfunctioning cash dispensers?

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is not working properly, so these letters fall out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A man in debt loves broken cash machines that pay out too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that these machines dispense cash only occasionally: a fruit machine is a gambling device with a single lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines pay out coins as jackpots, so they are whimsically called dispensers of cash, though they mostly take it.

clue.text: Incisive comment ultimately about new song

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word comment

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
a chant is a simple song, often repeated

explanation.surface: A critic makes a sharp remark about a new song.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean sharp and cutting, used of keen, forceful criticism or analysis.

clue.text: Feel good, bouncing back, full of this?

indicators.note: bouncing back says the hidden letters are read backwards
full of says the words Feel good contain the letters wanted, which sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone feeling good again after bouncing back is full of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'full of' unused: it is the hiding signal, and 'this' is the answer itself, which 'Feel good' is literally full of, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to joy or delight, the very feeling that someone who feels good is brimming with.

clue.text: Lettuce coated in sticky substance, syrupy stuff

indicators.note: the lettuce is coated in the sticky stuff, so its word goes inside the other

parts.note: glue is a sticky substance used for fixing things together
cos is a crisp, long-leaved variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: A salad leaf gets smeared with a gooey syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple sugar that is sold as a thick sweet syrup, used in confectionery.

clue.text: Dear old mate engaged in thought

parts.note: an ex is a former partner or spouse
someone pensive is engaged in deep thought

explanation.surface: A letter to a former partner who is lost in reflection begins 'Dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly or high-priced, as in 'petrol is dear this week'.

clue.text: Student of poetry will take part in discussion

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, so the student is one who cons
verse is poetry, writing in metrical lines

explanation.surface: A literature student is going to join a seminar debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'con verse', to study poetry: con is an old verb meaning to study carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk with someone, exchanging views, is to engage in conversation.

clue.text: Last in race, behind European crack racing team

indicators.note: behind places the final letter of race after the other pieces

parts.note: a crack is a witty remark or quip

indicators.note: Last in picks the final letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A crack racing team finishes last, trailing a European rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a team, used especially of teams in motor racing or cycling.

clue.text: Laugh at report about women's social media arrangement

indicators.note: about says the laughing word goes around the women's letter

parts.note: to titter is to laugh in a nervous, suppressed way
W is the standard abbreviation for women
an account is a report or description of events

explanation.surface: People snigger at a news report about women.
explanation.definitionFit: A user profile on the platform formerly called Twitter, the personal set-up for posting on that social network.

clue.text: Enclosure will accommodate most of men, female and me too

indicators.note: the envelope will accommodate the other pieces inside it

parts.note: SAE, a stamped addressed envelope, is often enclosed with a letter

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of men

parts.note: her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A paddock is big enough to hold most of the men, a woman and the speaker as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' looks like a pen or paddock, but here it is the SAE sent inside a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual reply agreeing that the speaker feels or does likewise; both phrases signal shared experience.

clue.text: Dessert page brought in plate, arranged with skill

indicators.note: the page letter is brought in among the letters of plate
arranged says those combined letters are put in a new order

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A dessert is set out on a plate with flair, and a page is sent in.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked pudding of pastry filled with fruit, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Worked out rough date and times

indicators.note: rough suggests a crude, approximate version, so these letters are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone calculated an approximate date and schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To have calculated or gauged an amount is to have reckoned it, if only approximately.

clue.text: Very fresh salmon is ace with the Chablis maybe

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
le is the French masculine for the
vin is French for wine, and Chablis is an example of a French wine

explanation.surface: A fresh salmon dish is perfect served with a glass of Chablis.
explanation.walkthrough: The French words match the French wine: LE VIN is 'the wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly hatched young salmon or trout, still carrying its yolk sac, is the freshest stage of the fish.

clue.text: To make fast progress, it's a mistake avoiding motorway

indicators.note: avoiding says the motorway's letters are kept out of the mistake word

parts.note: a misprint is a printing mistake, a typo
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A driver says it is wrong to stay off the motorway if you want to get somewhere quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it with the letter I standing in for the figure one.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or move at full speed over a short distance is to dash.

clue.text: Could this be viewed as 'female' film?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron and male means a man, so 'female' read in two parts gives the two halves of the title

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a film might be seen as one about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'female' as FE + MALE: FE is iron's chemical symbol and a MALE is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A 2008 Marvel superhero movie starring Robert Downey Jr as Tony Stark.

clue.text: Shopper has carrier filled with ale? The opposite

indicators.note: filled with would put the ale inside the carrier
The opposite reverses that, so the carrier goes inside the ale word instead

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a tray is a flat carrier for food and drinks

explanation.surface: A shopper's bag is apparently full of beer, or maybe the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is not a customer: in British slang, to shop someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shops a friend to the authorities is an informer, a traitor to them.

clue.text: Editor has last word on article from Germany

parts.note: amen is said as the last word of a prayer
der is a German definite article, meaning the

explanation.surface: A German editor gets the final say on a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One who alters or revises a text, correcting it, is doing the job of an editor.

clue.text: Briefly advise setter to make a fresh start

indicators.note: Briefly cuts the final letter from the word for advise

parts.note: to recommend is to advise a course of action
cement is something that sets hard

explanation.surface: A quick word of advice to the crossword setter: start again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is something that sets: cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning something again after a pause, a resumption, is a fresh start.

clue.text: Puzzle making you feel muddled quite regularly

indicators.note: quite regularly takes every second letter of the words feel muddled

explanation.surface: A tricky puzzle that leaves the solver feeling rather confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or escape someone's understanding, as a meaning eludes you, is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Name tag initially sewn into hat

indicators.note: the letter is sewn into the hat word, going inside it

parts.note: tile is an old slang word for a hat

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word tag

explanation.surface: A name label is first stitched into a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or work, or a word that names someone's rank.

clue.text: Creature making cat and sheep recoil

indicators.note: recoil means spring back, so the cat and sheep words run backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Something makes a cat and a sheep shrink back in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing rodent of the squirrel family, found in mountain regions, is one such animal.

clue.text: One tree planted by sister in swamp

indicators.note: planted by places the tree word beside the sister word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun is a sister in a religious order
the date palm is a tree

explanation.surface: A nun plants a single tree in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to flood or overwhelm, as water does land or work does a person.

clue.text: College admitted expelling learner

indicators.note: expelling throws the learner's letter out

parts.note: to let on is to admit or reveal something
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A school admitted it had expelled a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the English public school near Windsor; 'college' is part of its formal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous boarding school in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: Girl involved in attack around mid-morning, perhaps, is put off

indicators.note: the girl is involved in the turned word, going inside it
around turns the attack word back to front

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
she is a pronoun for a girl or woman
ten o'clock is an example of mid-morning

explanation.surface: A girl caught up in a mid-morning assault is unsettled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the attack word round to DIAR; 'mid-morning, perhaps' is a time of day, ten o'clock, not the middle letter of morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone, sapping their confidence or enthusiasm, is to put them off.
